items.title: Amazon CloudFront Announces HTTP/2 Support for Connections to Origins
items.content_snippet: Amazon CloudFront now supports HTTP/2 connections to custom origins and VPC origins. HTTP/2 lets CloudFront send many requests over fewer connections to your origin. This means fewer connections and TLS handshakes for your origin to handle, which improves performance for API and agentic workloads, such as AI agents calling MCP servers or mobile and web apps calling backend APIs. items.title: AWS Global Accelerator now preserves client IPs for NLBs with TLS listeners
items.content_snippet: AWS Global Accelerator now preserves the client IP address for traffic sent to Network Load Balancer (NLB) endpoints with TLS listeners. You can terminate TLS at your NLB and still see the original client IP address in your application. This means you can apply security groups, geo-blocking, rate limiting, fraud detection, audit logging, allowlists, and compliance controls based on the real client IP. items.title: Amazon Aurora serverless for MySQL now supports up to 384 ACUs
items.content_snippet: Amazon Aurora serverless now supports database capacity of up to 384 Aurora Capacity Units (ACUs) for Aurora MySQL-Compatible Edition, a 50% increase from the previous maximum of 256 ACUs. Each ACU provides approximately 2 gibibytes (GiB) of memory with corresponding CPU and networking, so a single Aurora serverless database can now scale up to 768 GiB of memory. items.title: Build the Workshop Before the Software Factory — Armin Ronacher, Earendil
items.content_snippet: Earendil's Pi coding agent has the same core tools it had a year ago, yet it does far more because the models got better. Armin Ronacher shows his own session data: fewer corrections, tasks running 14 minutes instead of two and a half, and 141 projects started but only 10 to 15 kept alive. His case: human attention is still the limit, so build a workshop that produces excellent software before building a factory that produces more of it.
